data.title: About -> Main
data.content:
We all passionately love athletics, the most elegant form of human activity and will probably follow it lifelong with a bunch of wondering, screaming or crying…

As a keen athletics enthusiast and journalist, I’ve been compiling various results for many years. Initially, I started recording some results in my notebook during my school years while at the same time copying all encyclopedia pages into it. But once I got my job 20 years ago, the compilation became easier for me.

Then I decided to gather all medallists in athletics history in one place: From South American juniors to Oceanian multi-eventers. That idea brought out Athleticspodium. My aim is simple: To have an open database that includes all major championships with all levels of competition.

TARGET: PROPER AND EASY INFO

I spent long days finding the correct medalists years after the competition ended, which may have changed several times due to doping offences or subsequent appeals. It’s really hard to find proper information, even on official websites or Wikipedia, which is the ‘shortest way’ to have results. The problem is, ‘old or false information’ is always available on the web, mixed with correct ones. We’re trying to solve this complexity with the help of all athletics lovers worldwide. It means the project was formed by me, but belongs to all athletics enthusiasts.

While compiling such a big data from very different sources, I learned many stories hidden between the pages. Also, these stories must not remain hidden in history. Athletics Podium will also aim to reveal the finest memories.

CONTENT: WHAT’S INCLUDED?

In the first phase of the project, we have mainly focus on championships. From Europe to Oceania, you can find all the top three medallists, results, technical data (wind, course measurement), and - if needed - some notes about the medal. We have all senior, U23, U20, and U18 podiums on the database. Athletics Podium offers you an easy way to trace the journey of athletes in the global athletics scene from the very beginning.

Also, Athletics Podium not only features great names in track and field but it also notices unsung heroes from different nations. It’s impossible to write articles about all the names registered in our database, but we’re sure it will become an encyclopedia of biographies during our research.

Simply, we are aiming for six topics in this project:

- (Most importantly) Verified information.

- Graphics that are easy to use for understanding the data. (On social media posts)

- Easy and free access to data. For everybody.

- Strong connection between rich athletics history & today.

- Broader collaboration for gathering information.

- Crediting every single contribution.

While I define myself politically as an 'eco-anarchist' or some kind of collectivist, I'm supporting open knowledge or free sources on the net. I don't have a copyright on such compiled material that actually belongs to everybody. Therefore, ALL RIGHTS ARE NOT RESERVED on this site. By bona fide effort, if you can put this site name as a source on your work in the case of excerpting data from our page, we'll be glad.

SHARE YOUR KNOWLEDGE

We are requesting your help in our quest to find the missing information listed here. After every single contribution, we put the names of those who help us by sending missing names, results, biography notes, name corrections, or photographs. Please use the nearby form to send your contribution to athleticspodium.com.

Let’s start to celebrate the athletics culture.

Sevket
